author.name: Data Dave
author.role: Builds secure, scalable data pipelines and manages storage infrastructure. Focuses on high-quality data operations and robust data governance. Collaborates on exploring data and managing data quality to support model development.

challenge.name: The Silent Store Gap
challenge.description: A batch of till scan lines from the northern stores was silently dropped during last night's ingestion, causing the model to forecast zero demand for fresh produce. #reliability_ruth# argues that the ingestion pipeline must be fully automated to guarantee every store's data arrives on time, while #data_dave# is willing to accept a manual verification step to ensure data quality before it reaches the feature store.

output.content: I am willing to accept a slower, manual verification step in the ingestion pipeline to ensure data quality before it reaches the feature store. This means we will not have fully automated data arrival for every store, and some batches may be delayed while we check for gaps. I am comfortable trading that speed for the certainty that the model does not learn from missing or corrupted scan lines. A silent drop like the one in the northern stores last night is a worse failure mode than a delayed load, because it corrupts the training signal for fresh produce demand. I would rather have a verified, slightly slower pipeline than a fast one that feeds the model zero demand for articles that actually sold.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states they are willing to accept slower, manual verification and delayed batches in exchange for the certainty that the model does not learn from corrupted or missing data.
